_comment: Domain -> normalized category. issuer_overrides encode the known disputes (e.g. Amex does not treat Instacart as a US supermarket). confidence: high|medium|low, shown in the popup. mcc_source records how a row was checked against the way purchases actually code: an issuer's own merchant list or a lookup of real statement codings, with the date. mcc, where present, is the Visa merchant category code that evidence names (e.g. a Chase label that is the code's own description). Rows without mcc_source are still unverified seed data.

instacart.com.note: third-party grocery delivery. Chase and Citi overrides removed 2026-09-28: both issuers count grocery delivery that codes as a grocery store or supermarket (chase.com rewards-category-faq; Citi Strata Premier terms), and Instacart charges are observed coding exactly that way on Chase ('Grocery stores and supermarkets') and Citi ('GROCERY STORE,SUPERMARKET') statements (awardwallet.com/merchants/Instacart_62245547, read 2026-09-28). amex kept: Amex's supermarket rate needs a merchant Amex classifies as a supermarket and its rewards-info pages do not say whether Instacart is one; Amex statements show it as 'Merchandise & Supplies - Groceries'. barclays: the JetBlue and other co-brand reward rules withhold bonus points from purchases made through third parties.

audible.com.note: Named in Prime Visa's 5% allowlist and missing from this table until 2026-09-10, which made that rule dead: audible.com resolved to no merchant, fell to `other`, and the card earned its 1% base. Category is online_retail because that is the rule the allowlist sits on, and because Audible sells digital goods. content_site is MEASURED 2026-09-10: the homepage carries Organization and FAQPage markup, og:type `book`, a price, no cart link and no buy control -- price only and nothing structural, which is the netflix.com shape, and one domain serves both the store and the player you listen in. Product pages carry Product and Offer, and commerce markup on the page beats content_site in isMerchantPage, so flagging darkens the homepage and the library while /pd/ pages and checkout still show. That is the opposite call from spotify.com for the opposite reason: Spotify's purchase surface has no markup to save it, Audible's does.
